question: The greatest common divisor of 119 and 56 is 7. Adding 14 gives 21 m/s velocity. A 35 kg mass has kinetic energy = 0.5 * 35 * 21^2, converted to kJ, scaled by 12 and by 6. A system pressure of 80 bar is not used here. What is the final energy in kJ?

The calculation 5*(3 + 10) = 65 gives velocity. A 18 kg mass has kinetic energy = 0.5 * 18 * 65^2, converted to kJ, scaled by 10, decreased by 16, increased by 21. A damping force of 50 N applies elsewhere. What is the final energy in kJ?

The second derivative of x^3 - 4x^2 at x = 2 is 4 m/s^2. A 131 kg mass produces force = 131 * 4 = 524 N, decreased by 7, scaled by 6, increased by 24, increased by 4. A safety threshold of 1000 N is noted. What is the final force in newtons?

Solving x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0 for the smaller root gives 1 m/s, scaled by 12 to get 12 m/s. A 43 kg mass has kinetic energy, scaled by 4, decreased by 25, and scaled by 10. A drag coefficient of 1.2 is not used. What is the final energy in joules?

Integrating 3x^2 + x from 2 to 4 gives an effective velocity (m/s). A 51 kg mass has kinetic energy increased by 17, converted to kJ, increased by 21, and decreased by 2. A maximum thrust of 100 kW is noted but not used. What is the final energy in kJ?

The greatest common divisor of 323 and 252 is 19. Scaling by 9 gives 171 m/s. A 60 kg mass with this velocity has kinetic energy, increased by 11, and converted to kJ. A reference altitude of 10000 m is not used. What is the final energy in kJ?

Sum k^2 for k from 1 to 5 equals 55. A 6 kg mass achieves this velocity in m/s. Kinetic energy is converted to kJ, scaled by 8, decreased by 4, decreased by 11. A reference pressure of 2 atm is not used. What is the final energy in kJ?

The derivative of 5x^3 - 4x^2 at x = 1 is 11 m/s^2. Scaling by 9 gives 99 m/s^2. A 31 kg mass experiences force = 31 * 99 N, converted to kN, increased by 18, and scaled by 3. A backup rating of 50 kN is noted. What is the final force in kN?

The greatest common divisor of 200 and 110 is 10 m/s. A 18 kg mass has kinetic energy scaled by 10, increased by 28, increased by 7, and converted to kJ. A temperature of 25 degrees C is not used. What is the final energy in kJ?

The combination C(12,2) = 66 represents channel count (m/s). A 11 kg mass has kinetic energy converted to kJ, increased by 2, decreased by 25, increased by 3. A bandwidth of 100 MHz is noted elsewhere. What is the final energy in kJ?

The derivative of x^3 - 2x^2 at x = 3 is 13. Decreasing by 10 gives 3 m/s^2. A 179 kg mass produces force, converted to kN, scaled by 7, decreased by 3. A thrust limit of 1000 kN is mentioned. What is the final force in kN?

The derivative of 2x^3 + x^2 at x = 3 is 63 m/s. A 60 kg mass has kinetic energy converted to kJ, scaled by 8 and 10, increased by 13. A rated speed of 100 m/s is specified. What is the final energy in kJ?

The second derivative of 5x^3 - 6x^2 at x = 1 is 18. Decreasing by 16 gives 2 m/s^2. A 162 kg mass produces force = 162 * 2, scaled by 4, converted to kN, scaled by 11. A safety factor of 2.0 is standard. What is the final force in kN?
Solving x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0 for the smaller root is 3 m/s^2. A 11 kg mass produces force = 33 N, scaled by 4 and 2 and 9. A damping coefficient is not used. What is the final force in newtons?

The combination C(8,4) = 70. Decreasing by 9 gives 61 m/s^2. A 170 kg mass produces force, converted to kN, decreased by 8. A reference acceleration of 9.8 m/s^2 is noted. What is the final force in kN?

Integrating 3x^2 + 2x from 0 to 1 gives 2 m/s. A 27 kg mass has kinetic energy increased by 1, converted to kJ, increased by 16, scaled by 2. A power rating of 100 W is elsewhere. What is the final energy in kJ?
Calculating 4*(7 + 18) - 23 = 77 m/s^2. A 8 kg mass produces force = 616 N, scaled by 2, decreased by 11, converted to kN. A system pressure of 10 bar is noted. What is the final force in kN?

Integrating x^2 + 6x from 2 to 4 gives 38 m/s. Decreasing by 21 gives 17 m/s. A 46 kg mass has kinetic energy decreased by 2, scaled by 2 and 8. A maximum velocity of 50 m/s is noted. What is the final energy in joules?

Solving x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0 for the larger root is 6 m/s^2. A 125 kg mass produces force = 750 N, scaled by 3, decreased by 28, scaled by 3, increased by 21. A threshold of 1000 N applies. What is the final force in newtons?

The greatest common divisor of 306 and 252 is 18 m/s. A 9 kg mass has kinetic energy scaled by 2, converted to kJ, decreased by 19, increased by 20. A reference density is not used. What is the final energy in kJ?

Solving x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0 for the larger root is 7 m/s. Decreasing by 1 gives 6 m/s. A 52 kg mass has kinetic energy scaled by 8 and 2, converted to kJ. A friction coefficient is not used. What is the final energy in kJ?
The greatest common divisor of 151 and 323 is 19 m/s^2. A 6 kg mass produces force = 114 N, converted to kN, scaled by 4 and 6. A maximum load of 1 kN applies. What is the final force in kN?
The derivative of 2x^3 + 3x^2 at x = 2 is 36 m/s^2. A 31 kg mass produces force = 1116 N, converted to kN, decreased by 15 and 19, scaled by 6. A backup is 50 kN. What is the final force in kN?
The calculation 4*(9 + 7) = 64 m/s. A 53 kg mass has kinetic energy decreased by 4, increased by 24, converted to kJ. A system limit is 200 kJ. What is the final energy in kJ?

Solving x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0 for the larger root is 7 m/s. A 50 kg mass has kinetic energy scaled by 12, decreased by 30, increased by 18, converted to kJ. A thermal rating is 100 C. What is the final energy in kJ?
